# Punt ST: Player Targets

**Summary.** Steals swing a lot from game to game and from season to season, so they are a sensible category to punt and a risky one to pay for in our 18 October auction. The punt ST targets in our data are mostly centers. Ivica Zubac is the one real anchor at a fair price. The rest are 1 to 3 USD late picks or waiver watches who bring FG%, rebounds, blocks and few turnovers.

## Why steals are a good punt

Steals are very variable from game to game and from season to season. Players whose value depends on steals carry extra risk. One expert ranks steals lower because they are low volume and unreliable. ([10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=863), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1534))

Steals and FT% are the two categories that change most from year to year. Even elite steals players can drop to 0.7 or 0.8 per game in a season. In our auction, do not pay extra for a player because of his steals. That part of his value is the least likely to hold. ([09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1346), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=794))

Punting a high-variance category costs less than punting a stable one. In head-to-head play you still win steals some weeks by luck, even with a weak steals roster. Points and assists are stable, high-volume categories and are bad to punt. Do not give up those categories to make room for steals. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722))

## How to run it in our league

Steals do not tie strongly to either the guard build or the big man build. So punt ST fits on top of whichever build you choose. Our target list leans toward centers, and the notes mention punt 3PM and punt AST as natural pairings for several of them. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=839), [Ivica Zubac](../profiles/players/ivica-zubac.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md), [Yves Missi](../profiles/players/yves-missi.md))

Steals are one of the most common categories on the waiver wire, and they distort standard 9-cat rankings. Before the draft, take players whose rank is inflated by steals out of your list, or mark them down. If you are not punting, you can still fill steals cheaply with FAB pickups during the season. You have up to 6 adds per week, so you do not need to buy steals at the auction. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1557))

The notes do not disagree on the main point. All of them call steals variable. They differ in what to do about it. One view is to punt steals outright, because you will still win the category in some weeks. The other view comes from steals being so common on waivers: that also makes them easy to stream later, so a manager who does not want to fully punt can just avoid paying for them in the auction. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1557), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1534))

## Zubac is the anchor

Ivica Zubac is the one punt ST target in our data who belongs in the middle of the auction. He anchors FG% and rebounds. His FT% is only a small drag because he takes few free throws. He fits both punt 3PM and punt ST. The note calls his Yahoo average cost a fair price but says his Yahoo value is too high. Last season he cost much more in our league and finished around 96th, so do not chase him up to last year's price. ([Ivica Zubac](../profiles/players/ivica-zubac.md))

Indiana has a weak 3-4-3 game schedule across our playoff weeks 19 to 21. That lowers his value for a title run. Early in the season, check whether Carlisle plays him more than 30 minutes or gives Jay Huff more of the time. ([Ivica Zubac](../profiles/players/ivica-zubac.md))

## Late-auction bigs for 1 to 3 USD

Khaman Maluach is close to our 144-player cutoff and should cost only 1 to 3 USD at the end. His value is blocks, with help in rebounds and FG%. Experts put his ceiling in the top 75. He fits punt AST and punt ST best. Check that he starts over Oso Ighodaro and plays 24 or more minutes while Mark Williams is out. ([Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md))

Yves Missi sits right at the cutoff and is a 1 to 2 USD pick for blocks. He adds FG% on low volume and has few turnovers. He averages about 0.4 steals, so he costs a punt ST team nothing. Check that he starts over Derik Queen and plays clearly more than last season's 19.6 minutes. If he does not, drop him to waivers. ([Yves Missi](../profiles/players/yves-missi.md))

Aaron Gordon is a 1 to 2 USD bench bid only if you punt both steals and blocks. In that build his average-plus line with a slight FG% edge fits. He played 51 and then 36 games in the last two seasons, and Denver may limit his minutes. Check his health and minutes early. If nobody drafts him, use him as a streamer. ([Aaron Gordon](../profiles/players/aaron-gordon.md))

Nikola Vučević is now a backup in Orlando. Pay 1 to 2 USD at most, and only as a late bench pick. He gives a center's rebounds with good FT% and few turnovers, but his blocks are thin. Check his minutes against Goga Bitadze under Sean Sweeney. Wendell Carter Jr.'s health is his only real route to top 100 value. ([Nikola Vučević](../profiles/players/nikola-vucevic.md))

Isaiah Stewart is a 1 USD final-round pick at most. He averages about 1.6 blocks and 0.3 steals and gives helpful FG% on low volume. Whether he is worth drafting depends on Zach Edey's foot. If Edey stays out, Stewart's starts make him worth a pick or an early waiver claim. If Edey is healthy, leave Stewart on waivers. ([Isaiah Stewart](../profiles/players/isaiah-stewart.md))

## Waiver watch list

Brook Lopez, Maxime Raynaud and Ryan Kalkbrenner fall outside our 144 drafted players. Do not draft them. Each one fits punt ST, but each needs more minutes before he is worth a FAB bid. ([Brook Lopez](../profiles/players/brook-lopez.md), [Maxime Raynaud](../profiles/players/maxime-raynaud.md), [Ryan Kalkbrenner](../profiles/players/ryan-kalkbrenner.md))

Lopez played 21.8 minutes last season and had no value. Add him only if he gets back toward 30 minutes, either because Isaiah Jackson loses the job or because of Clippers injuries. At that workload his blocks, threes and low turnovers could fill a streaming spot. Raynaud shoots efficiently and turns it over little, but at 19 to 20 minutes he will not hold value. Watch for Sabonis trade or injury news and for more three-point attempts. Kalkbrenner matters only if Diabaté loses the starting job or gets hurt. Then he becomes a short-term FG% and blocks pickup. ([Brook Lopez](../profiles/players/brook-lopez.md), [Maxime Raynaud](../profiles/players/maxime-raynaud.md), [Ryan Kalkbrenner](../profiles/players/ryan-kalkbrenner.md))
